Cp/volume capacity and conductivity are different experiments on the same product/conditioning population, without proof of the exact same physical coupon. Wet in the raw filenames denotes unconditioned indoor storage at 22 +/- 3 degC and relative humidity 40 +/- 20 percent, not water saturation or oven drying. Exact specimen moisture content is unreported. General HFM preparation makes planar specimens. Conductivity is measured through thickness with upward heat flow, generally following ASTM C518; heat capacity follows the general ASTM C1784-20 equal-plate temperature-step method. Applied contact pressure, material-axis mapping, instrument calibration uncertainty and cross-property covariance are not supplied. Three repeated conductivity cycles per specimen are not three extra independent specimens.

column4: Explicit arithmetic reduction following FSRI grouping; https://github.com/ulfsri/fsri_materials_database/blob/a432697e4b7d40f642b5cc8f384506439ebb32df/02_Scripts/plot_HFM_data_html.py
column5: Round recorded heat-capacity mean temperatures to 0.1 degC, as in the primary script; these rows group at 10,20,30,40 degC. Mean C_vol is the arithmetic mean of the three native volumetric readings at each group; add exactly 273.15 for kelvin. The computed replicate sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)) and is a separate TabulatedOnly statistic, not a confidence interval or calibration uncertainty. Extra computed digits represent arithmetic, not increased measurement resolution. Linear mean C_vol(T) and published Cp(T) interpolation is an authored approximation between the four groups with no measured interpolation-error bound or extrapolation. Native C_vol(T) needs no independent density(T).

The files PETG_Density_Wet_R1.csv, PETG_Density_Wet_R2.csv, PETG_Density_Wet_R3.csv report densities 1319,1312,1311 kg/m3, masses 141.4,141.2,140.6 g and volumes 107.2,107.6,107.3 cm3, respectively. The primary reduction uses the arithmetic mean of the reported rounded density column, 1314 kg/m3; recomputing mass/volume would change its inputs. Density test temperature is unspecified. Reference-normalization-density retains this algebraic input without temperature validity and is not a constant bulk-density law or density measured at every thermal knot. The material metadata headline is 1315 kg/m3, which differs from the CSV mean of 1314 kg/m3; this profile preserves the primary script input rather than substituting the headline.

FSRI divides each mean native C_vol by the common mean reported density and rounds to whole J/(kg K), yielding 1125,1166,1205,1245 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Its reported standard deviations 8,8,9,11 J/(kg K) are the native volume-capacity sample SD divided by that same mean density, rounded to whole units. Density scatter, calibration uncertainty and covariance are not propagated. Cp, C_vol and normalization density are algebraically related, not independent measurements. The published rounded Cp and SD values are retained exactly.

column4: Explicit interpretation of HFM apparent conductivity as a local scalar model
column5: Thermal-conductivity requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. This explicitly accepts substituting the measured apparent through-thickness conductivity at a finite nominal 20 K plate difference for a local conductivity at the same numerical temperature. It is an engineering approximation, not deconvolution of the plate temperatures or a new point measurement. Apparent-thermal-conductivity separately retains its native test-mean-temperature axis.
